_status: VERIFIED 2026-05-21 — four claims with different truth directions; labels derived from USPSTF, WHO, AHA, and established scientific literature. See _provenance per claim.

_provenance.claim-smoking: Smoking-CVD causal link: established 1964 US Surgeon General report, Doll & Hill cohort 1954/1964; AHA and USPSTF consistently classify as strong causal risk factor throughout all eras. Direction = SUPPORTS (evidence strongly supports the causal claim). Level = strong-for across all eras.
_provenance.claim-alcohol: Alcohol cardioprotection J-curve: widely reported 1990s–2015 (Ronksley 2011 BMJ, Di Castelnuovo 2006); guideline-endorsed as conditional benefit. REVERSED by Mendelian randomization studies 2016–2022 (Wood et al. 2018 Lancet 'no safe level of alcohol'; Biddinger 2022 JAMA Network Open; WHO 2023 joint statement). AHA 2021: 'We can't say moderate alcohol is cardioprotective'. Post-2018 era = REFUTES/conditional-against. NOTE: direction here is for the cardioprotection claim (positive hypothesis); SUPPORTS means evidence supports cardioprotection; REFUTES means evidence contradicts it.
_provenance.claim-hrt: HRT for cardiovascular prevention: pre-2002 observational studies favoured HRT (HERS pilot, WHI design era); USPSTF 2002 post-WHI E+P arm issued Grade D (recommends against) for chronic disease prevention; reaffirmed 2005 (E-alone), 2012, 2017, 2022. Direction = REFUTES (evidence refutes the cardioprotective prevention claim). Same fixture logic as hrt_uspstf.json.
_provenance.claim-obesity-paradox: Obesity paradox in established CVD: Lavie et al. 2003–2012 observational series reporting lower mortality in overweight/obese CAD patients; Flegal 2013 JAMA meta-analysis; challenged by methodological critiques (selection bias, weight-loss confounding, use of BMI). No major society guideline endorses prescribing overweight for CVD; NEUTRAL/no-recommendation throughout all eras studied. Still contested 2024 (Fothergill 2022, Zhang 2023).

_mapping_note: Claims extracted from the input text in order: claim-1=smoking, claim-2=alcohol, claim-3=HRT, claim-4=obesity-paradox. Direction is for the POSITIVE hypothesis as stated in the input (e.g., 'HRT reduces CVD risk' — evidence REFUTES this post-2002). The era transition years reflect: 2000 = pre-WHI, pre-MR; 2012 = post-WHI, alcohol-neutral or weak-support era; 2024 = post-MR alcohol reversal, HRT consistently D.
scope_note: Four cardiovascular claims deliberately spanning all three direction outcomes and one era-reversal. For internal engine calibration: a well-functioning ecology should converge toward SUPPORTS for smoking (stable), drift from SUPPORTS to REFUTES for alcohol (reversal), stay at REFUTES for HRT (consistent), and stay at NEUTRAL for obesity-paradox (contested). Multi-directional divergence, not mono-directional drift, is the signal of interest.

Unchanged; global evidence base only stronger
